speech_title: Remarks at the launch of the Dignity of Work Institute
main_topics: wages; productivity; cost of living; corporate power
major_quotes: "We see what's happened over the last 40 years. Corporate profits have soared, executive compensation has exploded, and productivity keeps going up and up, but wages aren't rising along with it, and the cost of living just keeps getting more expensive." / "In a nutshell, people can't keep up no matter how hard they work."
rhetorical_devices: four-decade frame; anaphora of rising/not-rising; plain-language summary ("in a nutshell")
policy_claims: Wage stagnation against rising productivity; a survey of registered voters commissioned by the institute found a quarter had worked more than one job in the previous two years
source: Ohio Capital Journal report quoting the press conference

speech_title: Statement on the LCV Action Fund endorsement
main_topics: environment; Great Lakes; East Palestine; lead exposure
major_quotes: "Ohioans have a right to clean air, safe drinking water, and a healthy environment... When Norfolk Southern's negligence contaminated East Palestine, I was there from day one holding them accountable and securing federal resources."
rhetorical_devices: rights framing; first-person presence claim ("I was there")
policy_claims: Great Lakes protection, clean-energy jobs, lead-paint and lead-pipe remediation

speech_title: Interview remarks on data centers and the NRSC memo
main_topics: data centers; utility rates; tax abatements
major_quotes: "Husted's been the front guy on all these data centers, 200 in Ohio, getting huge over-the-top tax breaks, and raising utility rates."
rhetorical_devices: synecdoche (Husted as "the front guy"); number as evidence ("200 in Ohio"); triple predicate
opponent_references: Husted by name, as the agent of the data-center build-out
policy_claims: Data-center tax abatements raise residential utility rates; 200 such facilities in Ohio (Brown's own count)

speech_title: Closing-argument remarks at a Westerville stop
main_topics: corporate money; big tech; oil companies; rigged system
major_quotes: "He's a special interest guy in Washington." / "The system is more rigged than before." / "I'll stand up to big tech. I'll stand up to the oil companies." / "Corporations and billionaires may try to buy this election for their golden boy, Jon Husted. But there are more of us than there are of them."
rhetorical_devices: antithesis (them/us); "golden boy" diminution; triple "I'll stand up to"; populist we-they frame
opponent_references: Husted named and characterised as a special-interest insider
policy_claims: Outside money is distorting the race; Brown positions himself against tech and oil interests

speech_title: Remarks at the Mahoning County Republican Party headquarters
major_quotes: "We changed the state... we took a state that was dying and made it a state that's now growing again, is now a place that people move to. It's a place where jobs are being created." / "My opponent, Sherrod Brown, has been in office for over 50 years. Can you name one thing that he's done to make your life better?" / "We have a tough campaign. Mid-term elections are elections where people maybe aren't as enthused to get out there and vote."
